input.quote: 2.7 Restrictions. Corio may not copy, distribute, reproduce, use or allow access to the Software or the MarketSite.net Service except as explicitly permitted under this Agreement
input.rationale: No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation binds Corio (our party). The grant clauses in Section 2 are all "nonexclusive" licenses to Corio (p0030, p0033–p0035), and the only restrictions on Corio (Section 2.7, p0042) are ordinary scope/reverse-engineering limits, not a covenant to source hosting or e-procurement software solely from Commerce One. Section 2.4 (p0035) grants Corio resale rights and constrains Commerce One from contacting Corio Customers directly — exclusivity-type protection running in our favor, which the playbook treats as acceptable. Exhibit D sales and marketing cooperation is expressly "non-binding" (p0198) and contains only a commercially-reasonable-efforts obligation to obtain two initial customer orders, not exclusive dealing. Section 13 (Shared Resources) creates no de facto exclusivity, and Exhibit B contains revenue-share percentages but no minimum purchase or requirements commitment. Note that several figures in Section 2.4 and Exhibit B are redacted ([*]); if the redacted text in Section 2.4 contains any exclusivity condition, this conclusion should be revisited on an unredacted copy. No redline required.
